scenario.brief: An online retailer is preparing for a major marketing campaign that is expected to create a large increase in customer traffic.
scenario.workload: The company runs a dynamic web application that currently depends on a single EC2 instance and a relational database.
requirements: Restrict direct access to application servers

questions.title: Distribute Incoming Traffic
questions.question: ShopWave currently runs its web application on a single EC2 instance. During major promotions, thousands of customers may arrive at the same time. Which AWS service should be introduced to distribute incoming application traffic across multiple EC2 instances?
questions.wrong_hint: Think about which AWS service sits in front of application servers and distributes incoming HTTP or HTTPS requests across multiple healthy targets.
questions.clue: Place a load balancer in front of the application servers so incoming traffic can be distributed across healthy instances.

questions.title: Scale with Demand
questions.question: ShopWave expects traffic to rise sharply during promotions and fall again afterward. The company wants the number of EC2 application servers to adjust automatically based on demand. Which AWS feature best meets this requirement?
questions.wrong_hint: Look for the AWS capability that automatically increases or decreases the number of EC2 instances as application demand changes.
questions.clue: Use an Auto Scaling group behind the load balancer so application capacity can grow and shrink with demand.

questions.title: Design for High Availability
questions.question: ShopWave must remain available even if an Availability Zone has a failure. How should the EC2 application tier be designed?

options.text: Run all EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone
Run the Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones
Replace the EC2 instances with Amazon S3

questions.wrong_hint: High availability means the application should not depend on a single Availability Zone.
questions.clue: Distribute application instances across multiple Availability Zones so the application can continue serving traffic if one zone has a failure.

questions.title: Choose the Database
questions.question: ShopWave stores customer and order data in a relational database. The team wants AWS to handle routine database tasks such as backups, patching and maintenance. Which service best meets this requirement?
questions.wrong_hint: The workload requires a relational database, and the team wants AWS to manage common database administration tasks.
questions.clue: Use a managed relational database so the application can store structured customer and order data without managing the database server itself.

questions.title: Protect the Application Tier
questions.question: ShopWave does not want customers on the internet to connect directly to its EC2 application servers. The servers should accept web traffic only from the Application Load Balancer. Which design best meets this requirement?

options.text: Allow HTTP and HTTPS from 0.0.0.0/0 directly to the EC2 instances
Configure the EC2 security group to allow application traffic only from the load balancer security group
Give every EC2 instance a public IP address
Disable security groups on the EC2 instances

questions.wrong_hint: The application servers should trust traffic coming through the load balancer rather than accepting web traffic directly from the internet.
questions.clue: Protect the application tier with security groups so EC2 instances accept application traffic only from the load balancer.
